turns.question: Have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed like this for weeks or months and then got better in between, or has this low mood been more or less constant for at least two years?

When you’re feeling at your lowest, have you had any hallucinations or very strong beliefs that others say aren’t true, such as hearing voices or feeling convinced you’ve done something unforgivable? Have you also had any thoughts of ending your life?
How has your sleep been over the past few months—are you sleeping much more or less than usual, or waking very early? Have you also noticed any change in your appetite or weight?

During that busy spell in the spring, did you feel unusually energetic or euphoric, more talkative or confident than usual, and need much less sleep without feeling tired? Did others notice you were acting differently or unusually driven?

Besides feeling overwhelmed, have you been feeling down or losing interest in things most days, or do these memory problems seem mainly tied to the stress of the divorce and move? When did the forgetfulness start in relation to those events?

When you were a child or teenager, did these attention and disorganization problems happen in more than one setting, like both at school and at home, and did they cause trouble with grades, behavior, or daily responsibilities?

Did those attention and organization problems also happen regularly at home or in other parts of your life when you were a child, not just at school? For example, were you often losing things, forgetting chores, or needing lots of reminders?

As an adult, do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one area of your life, like both at work and at home, or mainly during stressful periods related to the divorce and move? Have they been present pretty consistently even before the divorce?

Before the divorce, were these attention and organization problems causing clear problems in your daily life on a regular basis, or were they mostly manageable until the stress of the divorce made them much worse?

When you were a child, before the divorce-related stress of adult life, did your attention and forgetfulness cause clear problems outside school too, like at home, with friends, or in activities? If so, what kinds of problems do you remember?
Before age 12, did your attention or forgetfulness cause clear problems in any setting other than school, like at home, with chores, friendships, or activities? If yes, what do you remember?

Do you have anyone or anything that could confirm these attention problems were present before age 12 in daily life, such as a parent, sibling, old report cards, or school records? Or do you think the current problems are mainly a reaction to the divorce and increased responsibilities?

When life was less stressful before the divorce, did these attention problems still cause noticeable trouble at work, managing your home, or relationships, or were they only a real problem after the divorce? Please give one or two examples.
Before age 12, do you remember these attention problems causing any clear difficulties outside of school, like at home, in sports, hobbies, or with friends? If yes, what happened?

Since the divorce and move, have these problems eased as the stress settled, or have they stayed about the same even when things are calmer? Also, before the divorce, did you ever have similar attention problems cause mistakes or missed responsibilities at work or in managing adult life?

Before age 12, did a parent, sibling, or anyone else ever notice that you were also forgetful, disorganized, or needed lots of reminders at home—not just at school? If so, what do you remember them saying or doing?

Between the divorce and move 11 months ago and your lifelong tendency to space out, which feels more true: that stress mainly made an old attention problem much worse, or that these problems only really began because of the divorce? Before the divorce, can you name one adult example of this causing a mistake or missed responsibility, even if it was milder?

If the divorce-related stress were to settle down and your responsibilities became lighter again, do you think these attention problems would mostly go back to being minimal, or would they still clearly interfere with daily life? What makes you think that?

Before the divorce, when life was more stable, did your attention problems still cause clear difficulties in at least two areas of adult life, like work, home, finances, or relationships? If yes, what were they?

Before the divorce, even if things felt manageable overall, did your lifelong spacing out or disorganization ever cause smaller but real problems in adult life—like late bills, missed appointments, losing important items, or mistakes at work? Please give one specific example if you can.

Outside of the divorce and move, have you ever had another period in your adult life when stress was low but you still had the same attention problems causing real impairment? If yes, what was one example?

During the 11 months since the divorce, have your forgetfulness and disorganization been present almost every day, or do they mainly flare up when you’re feeling stressed or thinking about the divorce? When you have a calmer day, do these problems noticeably improve?

Do you still have any old report cards or can a parent/sibling confirm that, before age 12, these attention problems also caused trouble outside school—like at home, with chores, or in activities? If yes, what specific problems were noticed?

Before age 12, even if you don’t remember details, did anyone ever tell you that you were also forgetful, disorganized, or needed repeated reminders at home or in activities outside school? If yes, who said it and what did they notice?

When you forget bills or appointments now, is it usually because you’re distracted by thoughts or emotions about the divorce, or does it feel like the same kind of spacing out you’ve had since childhood even when you’re not upset? Which of those fits better most of the time?

Before age 12, can you think of any non-school example of this same spacing out or forgetfulness causing a problem, like losing things during activities, forgetting plans, or needing repeated reminders at home? If so, what happened?

Is there a parent, sibling, or anyone who knew you as a child that we could ask whether you had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities before age 12? If yes, what do you think they would say?

Since the divorce, have you also had symptoms like constant sadness, anxiety, trouble sleeping, or repeatedly thinking about the divorce, or is the main problem still the same lifelong inattention and disorganization? Which feels like the bigger issue day to day?

Before age 12, besides school, did these same attention problems clearly cause trouble in any other setting, like at home, with chores, sports, hobbies, or friendships? If yes, please give one specific example.

Can you ask a parent, sibling, or someone who knew you well as a child whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities before age 12? What do you think they would say?

To help tell whether this is lifelong ADHD or mainly stress-related, can you ask a parent, sibling, or someone who knew you before age 12 whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or during activities outside school? If so, what did they notice?

Would you be willing to check with a parent, sibling, or old records to find out whether, before age 12, you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities outside school? If yes, what did they notice?
Before age 12, can you check with a parent or sibling and ask whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or during activities outside school? What do they remember?

Do these repeated checks feel driven by unwanted thoughts or fears that something bad will happen if you don’t check, or do they feel more like your usual way of being careful and perfectionistic? Also, do you recognize the checking as excessive or unreasonable?

Which is more distressing and time-consuming for you overall: the unwanted intrusive thoughts and images themselves, or the repeated checking rituals you do to relieve them? If you had to choose, which one feels like the main problem?

Have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks and then got better in between? Or did this start mainly after a specific stressful event or major life change?

How much is this affecting your daily life—are you still able to manage basic things like getting out of bed, bathing, eating, and keeping up with responsibilities? Have you had any experiences like hearing your mother’s voice when no one is there or feeling so hopeless that you’ve thought about ending your life?
Do you see yourself as overweight or have an intense fear of gaining weight, even if other people say you are underweight? Also, has your weight become significantly low for your age and height?

When you feel you’ve eaten too much, are there times you eat a clearly large amount of food in a short period and feel unable to stop or control it? Or do you mainly purge or restrict after normal-sized meals because of fear of weight gain?
After these binge episodes, what do you usually do to try to prevent weight gain—such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or exercising excessively?
When you were a child or teenager, did you also have trouble paying attention, staying organized, or sitting still at school or home? Or did these problems mainly start later in adulthood?
Do these attention and impulsivity problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home or in social situations? Can you give one or two examples?

Have these attention and impulsivity symptoms caused clear problems in your life, such as poor grades, job loss, accidents, money trouble, or relationship conflict? What is the biggest example that stands out?

When your focus and organization get worse, is that mainly during times when you’re depressed, very anxious, or using alcohol/drugs, or are these problems pretty constant even when your mood is okay? Have there been long stretches when your mood was fine but the attention problems were still clearly there?

Have you had problems since childhood with being restless, interrupting, or having trouble focusing and waiting your turn across different settings like school, work, and home, or did this pattern start later mainly around intense relationships or urges?

Have these unusually high, on-edge moods ever started during or soon after using alcohol, recreational drugs, or stimulant medications like Adderall or cocaine? Or do they happen even when you haven’t used any substances?

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in most things most of the day, nearly every day? If so, did that happen before or between these high-energy periods?

During these high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or strongly believed things that others said were not true, like having special powers or being watched? If yes, did that only happen when your mood was extremely high?

When you felt you were on the verge of a field-changing breakthrough, did other people see that belief as clearly unrealistic or out of touch with reality? Also, have you had any other experiences during these times, like hearing or seeing things others didn’t?

When you cut back on food, is it mainly because you’re afraid of gaining weight or feel your body is too big, or is it more because unwanted repetitive thoughts or rules make you feel you have to do it even if it’s not about your weight?

Have you become significantly underweight for your age and height because of this restriction, or are you still in a normal weight range? Also, even if others say you are too thin, do you still feel fat or believe you need to lose more weight?
After these episodes of eating large amounts, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? If so, how often does that happen?
How often do these nighttime episodes of eating very large amounts happen, and for how many months has this been going on?
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating? Or is it more that you choose to eat then because you’re lonely or upset?
Since the plant accident, have you been having unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about it, and has this been going on for more than a month?

Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel out of control while doing it? If so, do you then try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

What is your current height and weight, or have you been told you are significantly underweight? This helps me tell whether these binge-and-purge episodes are happening at a very low body weight or not.

What is it that you keep trying to fix before going out—are you mainly worried about a flaw in your appearance, doing certain rituals until they feel right, or being judged by other people? Which of these feels most true for you?

When these rituals happen, are they mainly driven by fears that your appearance looks defective or ugly, or do you also have unwanted thoughts and rituals about things not related to your looks? If there are non-appearance thoughts, what are they about?
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest, and has it been a single continuous period or have there been separate episodes with times in between when you felt back to normal?

During those few days when you feel really revved up, do you also need much less sleep and feel unusually confident, talkative, or impulsive compared with your usual self? Have these periods ever lasted 4 days or more?

During your low periods, have there been times lasting at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest most of the day nearly every day, along with other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt, or thoughts of death?

Have you been having sudden episodes of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, dizziness, or feeling like you might lose control that peak within minutes? Or is it more of a constant worry that stays with you most days?
How long have you been feeling this constant worry and tension most days? Did it start after a specific stressful event, or has it been going on for 6 months or longer?

If your work situation improved or the promotion-related pressure went away, do you think the worry would mostly disappear, or do you tend to worry excessively about many areas of life even apart from that stress? Has this kind of broad, hard-to-control worrying happened to you before this job change?

Since this started after your promotion, do the worry and tension still feel mostly tied to that work stress, or do they now seem excessive and hard to control even when you’re not thinking about the promotion? Have these symptoms continued even during times when work pressure briefly eased up?

Before the promotion, were you generally a worrier, or did this pattern of excessive worry begin only after that stress and stay closely linked to it? In other words, does it feel like a reaction to that life change, or more like a new ongoing anxiety problem of its own?

Along with the worry, have you been having symptoms like trouble sleeping, feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, irritability, trouble concentrating, or getting tired easily? How much are these symptoms affecting your daily life at work, at home, or socially?
Since the collapse, do you also have unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about it? Or does the panic mainly happen only when you’re near buildings or unfinished structures?
Do these sudden panic episodes ever come out of nowhere when you’re not near buildings or reminded of the collapse, or do they only happen when something triggers memories of that event?
Before this promotion, did you have similar problems with focus, organization, or forgetfulness going back to childhood or school years? Or did these difficulties start only after the job change?

Do these attention and organization problems affect you in other parts of life too, like at home, with bills, appointments, or relationships, or are they mainly a problem only at this job? Also, do you feel constantly worried and tense most days even when there isn’t a specific stressor?
Since the electrical shock at work, do you have unwanted memories or nightmares about it, or do you avoid reminders of what happened? Also, about how long has this been going on?

Have you ever had a brain injury, stroke, seizure disorder, or another neurological illness before these problems started? Or has this mainly felt like stress and anxiety without any known medical cause?

Besides getting mixed up at work, have you been feeling anxious or worried most days about a lot of different things, and is it hard to control that worry? Do you also notice symptoms like feeling on edge, muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or irritability?

When this happens at work, do you know what you want to do but your body seems to do the steps in the wrong order, or is it more that anxiety makes you freeze or panic? Can you give me one specific example?

When these episodes happen, do you ever lose the ability to move part of your body or have weakness, tremors, or trouble walking, or is it mainly the odd, disorganized movements and postures? Have you ever become unable to speak or had changes in vision or sensation during them?

When these episodes happen, do you feel aware of what you’re doing but unable to stop or control it, or does it feel automatic or unreal, like it’s happening without your control? Do they tend to start more when you’re under stress or when other people are around?

Right before these episodes started, was there a major conflict, trauma, or stressful event, and do the episodes ever seem to help you avoid work or get extra attention or support? Also, when the episode ends, do you remember it clearly the whole time?

Have you been hearing voices or feeling that people are controlling your movements or thoughts? Also, have others noticed you staying still in unusual postures for a long time or repeating words or movements?

When you suddenly stop or hold a strange posture, how long does it usually last, and if someone asks you to move or guides you, can you respond normally or do you stay stuck? Do you ever repeat other people’s words or movements?

Outside of these odd postures and pacing, have you also had times of barely speaking, not moving unless pushed, refusing to eat or drink, or resisting when people try to reposition you? Have you noticed this happening for days at a time?

Have you had any other schizophrenia-like symptoms, such as feeling people are watching or plotting against you, or your thoughts becoming jumbled or hard to follow? Before these movement problems started, did you notice a drop in motivation, emotions, or self-care?

How long have the disorganized behavior and jumbled thinking been going on, and have they been present most days for at least 1 month? During this time, has your work or daily functioning clearly gotten worse than it was before?
Before this current high-energy period, have you ever had a past episode of depression or a similar high/overactive episode? If so, were you ever diagnosed with bipolar disorder?

During this current high-energy episode, have you been hearing or seeing things other people don’t, or strongly believing things that others say aren’t true? If yes, did those experiences happen only while your mood was unusually high?

Since the highway scare, do you keep having unwanted memories or nightmares about it, or find yourself avoiding driving or anything that reminds you of it? Have you also been feeling down most of the day nearly every day, even aside from thinking about the event?
How long has it been since the highway scare, and have these nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance, and numb mood been happening for more than a month?
During the highway scare, did you believe you were about to die or be seriously injured, or was it mainly a very stressful event without that level of danger? Did anyone actually get hurt?

Since the highway scare, have these symptoms started to get better at all, or are they staying just as strong and interfering with your daily life? Have you been able to function at work and in relationships, or is it causing major impairment?

Since the symptoms began, have there been any periods of at least a few days when the nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance clearly eased up, or have they stayed intense the whole time? Also, are you now past one month since the highway scare?

Since the highway scare, have you felt detached from yourself or like the world around you seems unreal or dreamlike? Or does it mostly feel like fear, nightmares, and avoidance without that sense of unreality?

During the highway incident, was there an actual crash or another event that truly threatened your life or could have caused serious injury, or was the main danger the feeling that you were having a heart attack? Also, did any doctor later confirm a real medical emergency?

At the time on the highway, was there any actual external danger—like a crash, loss of control of the car, or another life-threatening event—or was the fear mainly that you were dying from what felt like a heart attack? This helps me tell whether the event itself meets the kind of trauma exposure we look for.

Before this highway episode, had you ever had sudden panic attacks or intense episodes of chest tightness, shortness of breath, or fear of dying that came out of the blue? Or was this the first time anything like that ever happened?

Since that first episode on the highway, have you had any other sudden panic attacks that came out of the blue, not triggered by reminders of the event? Or do the intense fear episodes only happen when something reminds you of that night or of being far from medical help?

Since the highway episode, have you had repeated panic attacks that seem to come out of nowhere even when you are not reminded of that night or worried about your health? Or do they only happen when something triggers memories of the event or fear of being far from medical help?

Since the highway episode, have you had any full panic attacks that truly came out of the blue, with no reminder of that night and no health-related worry beforehand? Or do they always happen in connection with memories of the event or fear about your body or being far from medical help?

Since the hospital told you your heart was fine, do you still spend a lot of time worrying that you have a serious heart problem despite reassurance? Or is your fear mainly about reliving that highway episode rather than believing you’re currently medically ill?

On a typical day, what takes up more of your mind: fear that you currently have a serious heart condition despite normal tests, or fear and memories of reliving that highway episode? Which one is driving your avoidance and distress the most right now?

If you were close to a hospital and felt confident help was immediately available, would you still avoid travel or public places because you might panic or be unable to escape? Or would the avoidance mostly go away?

Since the hospital said your heart was healthy, have you been repeatedly checking your body, seeking reassurance, or looking up heart symptoms because you still believe you may have a serious illness? Or is the fear mainly about having another episode like that night rather than believing you currently have heart disease?

If your doctor repeated the tests today and again showed your heart is healthy, would your fear and avoidance mostly go away, or would you still keep worrying and checking because you might have a serious illness? This helps me tell whether the main problem is ongoing illness fear or reliving that highway episode.

During the times this has been happening, have you also had periods of feeling unusually high or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or unusually increased energy? If so, did those mood changes start before or around the same time as these beliefs?

Aside from these beliefs, have you ever heard voices or seen things others don’t, or had trouble organizing your thoughts, speech, or daily functioning? Have you also noticed reduced motivation, emotional expression, or social withdrawal not explained by stress?

Do you believe these people are harming your career through ordinary real-world actions, or through impossible things like reading your thoughts, controlling your mind, or sending special messages meant only for you?

Has there ever been a time in these two years when you seriously considered that your interpretation might be mistaken, or are you completely certain this coordinated sabotage is happening? What evidence makes you most sure?

Have any of these people ever directly threatened you, admitted they were coordinating against you, or have you found clear objective proof others could verify? Or is your certainty based mainly on interpreting events like delays, lost materials, and schedule changes as connected?
Did this anxiety start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or has it been more of an ongoing pattern? About how long has it been going on?

Besides work, do you also find yourself worrying a lot about other parts of life, like your health, family, finances, or everyday responsibilities? Or is the anxiety mainly limited to your job and sales targets?

Along with the constant worrying, have you also had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, or problems sleeping? If so, which ones have been happening most days?

How much is this anxiety affecting your day-to-day functioning—for example, your work performance, relationships, or ability to handle routine tasks? Have you been avoiding anything or missing work because of it?

Have you been using a lot of caffeine, energy drinks, alcohol, cannabis, or any medications or drugs that seem to make the anxiety worse? Do you have any medical problems like thyroid issues or heart symptoms that started around the same time?

Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or physical symptoms—like your heart racing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, dizziness, or feeling like you might lose control—that peak within minutes? Or is the anxiety more of a steady, ongoing worry throughout the day?

During these years of feeling down, have there been stretches of 2 months or longer when your mood felt mostly normal? Also, have you had any separate periods when the depression became much worse than your usual baseline for at least 2 weeks?

Have there been times lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, and were more impulsive or talkative than usual? Or has this restlessness mainly been a long-standing pattern for you, especially since childhood?
Besides work, do these attention or hyperactivity symptoms also cause problems in other parts of your life, like at home, in relationships, or during hobbies? Can you give one or two examples?

Along with the restlessness, do you also often have trouble paying attention or staying organized, like losing things, forgetting tasks, or making careless mistakes? If so, did those problems also start in childhood?

During these times when you feel sped up and out of control, have you had things like hearing voices or strongly believing things others said weren’t true, and have you ever also had a separate period of at least two weeks where you felt very depressed or lost interest in almost everything?
How long have you been feeling that people in town are targeting you, and have you also been hearing voices or seeing things that others don’t?

Since this started, have you had trouble thinking clearly, speaking in a way others find hard to follow, or taking care of yourself like bathing, cooking, or keeping up with daily tasks? Have your emotions felt unusually flat or your motivation dropped a lot?

Did these concentration and self-doubt problems begin after a specific stressful event or change at work or in your life, or have they been building up more generally over time? Have you also been feeling down or losing interest in things most days?

Do you feel down and uninterested most of the day nearly every day even outside of work, or do these feelings mainly happen when you’re dealing with the stressful project? Have they continued even when the work stress eases?

During your “high” periods, have you ever had at least 4 days in a row of clearly increased energy or unusually elevated or irritable mood with less need for sleep, talking more, racing thoughts, or impulsive behavior? If so, did those times cause obvious problems or lead to hospitalization?
Since the car accident, have these symptoms lasted less than a month or more than a month? Also, are you having nightmares, flashbacks, or avoiding reminders of the accident?

During the accident or afterward, did you ever feel numb, detached from yourself or your surroundings, or like things weren’t real? Have these symptoms stayed only within the first month since the accident?

Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel out of control, and if so, do you then do anything to prevent weight gain such as vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise?
Have you become significantly underweight because of this restriction, or is your weight still within or above the normal range for your height?
How long has it been since the car drove into the crowd, and have these symptoms lasted more than a month?

Since the accident, have you had moments where you felt numb, detached from yourself, or like things around you weren’t real? Have there been times you couldn’t remember important parts of what happened?
Since the accident, have you been having unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about what happened, or do you find yourself avoiding reminders of the street fair?
Since the accident happened only a week ago, have there been any periods when these symptoms completely went away, or have they been present most of the time every day since then?
Have you had other periods in the past when you felt depressed like this and then got better in between, or has this low mood been more or less constant for at least two years?

When you’re in these low periods, do you ever hear or see things others don’t, or have very strong beliefs that others say aren’t true? This helps me tell whether the depression includes psychotic symptoms.
How long have these memories of the explosion been coming back like this? Did they start within the past month, or have they been going on for more than a month?

Since the explosion, have you been going out of your way to avoid reminders of it, like certain places, conversations, or activities? Do you also find yourself trying to push away thoughts or feelings about what happened?

Since the explosion, have you started feeling persistently guilty, numb, detached from other people, or like you’ve lost interest in things you used to care about? Have you also found yourself blaming yourself or feeling like the world is no longer safe?

Since the explosion, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled, and have you had problems with sleep, irritability, or concentrating? These can help me understand how much your body is still reacting to what happened.

During this time, have you also had a period of feeling extremely high or unusually energetic, or the opposite—very depressed most of the day? If yes, did those mood changes happen at the same time as the voices?
How long have you been hearing these voices and having trouble functioning—did it all start within the last month, or has it been going on for longer than a month?

Besides hearing the voices, have you also strongly felt that people are spying on you, trying to harm you, or sending you special messages? Have you noticed your thoughts becoming jumbled or your speech hard for others to follow?

Before the voices and feeling watched started four months ago, during that earlier several-month decline, were you already having odd beliefs or hearing things, or was it mainly loss of motivation, reduced interest, and trouble functioning? Have those low-drive symptoms continued even when the voices are less intense?

Have you had similar problems with attention, organization, or finishing tasks since childhood or your school years, or did this start only recently? Also, do you often feel persistently worried or down most days?
Besides work, do these attention or restlessness problems also affect other parts of your life, like managing chores, finances, appointments, or relationships? Can you give one or two examples?
Besides feeling that people at work are plotting against you, have you been hearing voices or noticing your thoughts or speech becoming confused or hard to follow? If so, when did that start?
How long have you been convinced that your coworkers are plotting against you? Did this start suddenly over days to weeks, or has it been going on for several months or longer?

During this past year, have you also had long periods of feeling very depressed or unusually energetic with much less need for sleep? If yes, did those mood changes happen at the same time as your belief about your coworkers?

Have you had other separate periods like this in the past where you felt depressed or lost interest for weeks or months and then got back to your usual self in between? Or has this low mood and loss of interest been present most of the time for at least two years without really letting up?

During this depression, have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or strongly believed something that others said wasn’t true? This includes voices, visions, or fixed beliefs like being ruined or guilty in a way that felt absolutely certain.

How much has this depression affected your ability to function day to day—for example, are you still able to work, take care of yourself, and manage basic responsibilities, or has that become very difficult or impossible?
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life? If yes, have you made any plans or taken any steps toward it?

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or did risky things that were out of character? Even if it happened at a different time than this depression.

During this depression, how have your sleep and appetite changed—are you sleeping much more or less than usual, and have you noticed weight loss or gain? Also, has your energy or ability to concentrate been affected?

During the times when you’re full of plans, do you also need much less sleep, feel unusually energetic or confident, or get more talkative or impulsive than usual? How long do those periods usually last?

During your low periods, have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 weeks where you felt depressed most of the day or lost interest in most things, along with symptoms like sleeping or eating changes, low energy, guilt, or trouble concentrating? Or are the lows more of a chronic, milder gloominess without a clear major depressive episode?

During those high-energy weeks, did your symptoms ever become severe enough that you were hospitalized, had psychotic symptoms like delusions or hallucinations, or caused major problems at work, finances, or relationships? If so, what happened?

Did these changes start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without any clear trigger? Have you had other similar episodes of losing interest or feeling depressed in the past?

Since that stressful school year ended or changed, have your low mood and loss of interest improved at all, or have they continued even without the stress being as intense? Also, do these symptoms still feel closely tied to work stress, or do they now feel present most of the time regardless of what is happening?

Over the past two weeks, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? Which of these have been present for you?

Along with losing interest and motivation, have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least the past two weeks? Or is it more a sense of emptiness and lack of drive without feeling particularly sad?
Before this started 14 months ago, were there at least 2 years when you felt down, empty, or unmotivated most days? Or was your mood and motivation basically normal until this began?

How much has this loss of interest and motivation affected your day-to-day functioning at work and home? For example, are you still able to keep up with teaching, chores, and basic responsibilities, or are you falling behind?

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true? Even when you know you’re not feeling like yourself, has anything like that happened during this period?

When you hear these voices or think the curriculum was designed to target you, do they fit with your feelings of failure and loss of motivation, or do they seem unrelated to your mood? Have you had any other unusual beliefs or experiences outside of this depressive period?
Is your fear mainly triggered by being in high places, and do you avoid them or endure them with intense anxiety even when you know the danger is small?
Did these feelings start after a specific work or life stress, or have you been feeling this way most days even without one? About how long has this been going on?
